.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r16/task/tests/app_context.md and the five prompt.md files (searched for clock/date/time rules)
evidence: Judge agent and model: task/task.toml [verifier.env] is REWARDKIT_JUDGE = "claude-code", REWARDKIT_MODEL = "z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx", ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL = "https://openrouter.ai/api", ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}", ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "" - identical to the frozen block in staged-task-contract.md lines 66-71; diff of task.toml against the frozen template shows only name/description/keywords/difficulty/category/provenance/arena_slice lines differ. All five judge.toml files carry only the expected `judge = "claude-code"` fallback and no model, temperature or reasoning-effort key (grep for model|temperature over tests/**/judge.toml returns nothing); the [judge] and [[judge.mcp_servers]] header of every judge.toml is identical to the template's (diff up to the first [[criterion]]). CLIs and browser: task/tests/Dockerfile is byte-identical (CR-insensitive diff) to the template and pins `@anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.281`, `@openai/codex@0.151.0`, `@playwright/mcp@0.0.79`, `express@5.1.0`, `better-sqlite3@12.4.1`, `harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7`; Chromium is installed by the Playwright CLI bundled inside the pinned @playwright/mcp (`PW_CLI="$(npm root -g)/@playwright/mcp/node_modules/playwright/cli.js" ... install --with-deps chromium`), so the browser build follows that pin, and every judge.toml launches it via `--executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium`. Shared tools: tests/test.sh, tests/tools/restart_mcp.py, tests/tools/score.py, tests/scoring.toml and tests/.dockerignore are identical to the frozen template; test.sh and tools contain no curl/wget/npx/pip/npm fetch at grading time. Fixed clock: the task has no graded calendar or run-date rule. A search of all criteria, prompts, app_context.md, instruction.md and /instructions notes for clock/today/date/timestamp/created_at/UTC finds no criterion that compares a date or depends on the run date; the seed is `"snippets": []` with no dated rows. The only time language is relative durations the judge waits out (e.g. functional judge.toml line 299 `within about ten seconds a visible time-limit reason must appear`, line 389 `watch its library for up to ten seconds`), which are independent of the run date, so the fixed-clock clause has nothing to bind. Evidence index: all 16 scripted-golden artifact hashes match raw bytes and all 6 hosted-run JSON hashes match LF-normalised bytes. The hosted run on the EARLIER candidate records `"model": "z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx"` in verifier/scored/reward-details.json, showing the same shared verifier wiring resolves to the pinned model; that is not a measurement of these bytes, and no verifier-image build or configured judge run exists for these bytes (not required to decide this static pinning row). Notes, not defects: (1) base images are pinned by tag, not digest (`node:22-bookworm-slim`, `python:3.12-slim`) and apt packages plus Playwright `--with-deps` are unversioned - template-controlled, and the workbook's deterministic row treats unpinned apt as a NOTE; (2) the model is pinned by OpenRouter slug, whose upstream serving provider is not fixed, and no temperature is set - the row explicitly says temperature and prompt-version markers are not required; (3) several criteria depend on wall-clock waits of 2-10 seconds performed by an LLM judge, a source of run-to-run judge variance that belongs to the criterion-quality rows rather than this pinning row. Probe: an app that derives behaviour from the run date gains or loses nothing, since no criterion reads a date; a conforming app is not exposed to a moving clock. Open verifier network is not a defect per the row text.
